to set something aside.definition: to decide not to consider something for now, so you can focus on something else

a by-product of.definition: something that happens as a side effect of a process that was aimed at something else

in principle / in practice.definition: in principle = according to the theory or the rules; in practice = in what really happens

to be agnostic about.definition: to deliberately take no position on a question

to hold up under.definition: to stay true or valid when tested or put under pressure

to over-generalize from.definition: to draw a broad conclusion from too few or too special cases

an upper / lower bound on.definition: a value that a quantity can never be above (upper) or below (lower)

to be at ceiling.definition: (of test scores) to be at or near the maximum, so the test can no longer show differences

a talking point, not a result.definition: an idea worth discussing, but not strong enough to count as evidence

the burden of proof lies with.definition: the person making a claim is the one who must show evidence for it

to read too much into something.definition: to find more meaning or importance in something than it really has

on the face of it.definition: judging from how it first looks (often followed by a 'but')

that’s a big if.definition: the condition you just mentioned is uncertain or unlikely

to boil down to / to hinge on.definition: boil down to = to be, in its most basic form; hinge on = to depend completely on

to cut both ways.definition: to have effects or implications for both sides of an argument

to tease apart.definition: to separate things that are mixed together so you can study each one

to stop short of.definition: to come close to doing or saying something but not actually do it

a far cry from.definition: very different from (usually much worse or less than)

a bit of a stretch.definition: a claim or description that goes further than the facts allow

to take something with a grain of salt.definition: to treat a claim with some doubt and not fully believe it

the jury is still out (on).definition: people have not yet reached a decision or agreement (about)

to lend weight to.definition: to make an idea or argument more convincing

to give someone pause.definition: to make someone stop and think carefully, often with doubt

as a rule of thumb.definition: as a practical, approximate rule based on experience

to sidestep a question.definition: to avoid dealing with a question directly

Hedging ladder.definition: verbs ordered from strongest to weakest claim: shows > indicates > suggests > is consistent with > hints at

Concession, then your point.definition: accept part of the other view first (Granted, … / While it is true that …), then make your own point (But …)

Cleft sentence for focus.definition: What X did was Y / It is X that Y: puts the stress on the most important part

Inversion for emphasis (writing, formal.definition: after Not only / Only when / Rarely, put the auxiliary verb before the subject for emphasis

research (uncountable).definition: research is uncountable: do research / a study, not a research or researches

discuss / explain.definition: discuss takes a direct object; explain takes 'to' before the person
discuss / explain.wrong: discuss about the result; explain me
discuss / explain.right: discuss the result; explain it to me

in my view.definition: use 'in my view' or 'as I see it'
in my view.right: in my view; as I see it

a / the.definition: the = one specific thing both sides know; a = one of many; no article = things in general
a / the.wrong: entropy of the English (in general statements)
a / the.right: the entropy of English; a model of text; language models (in general)
